summary: Decentralized lending protocol on Cronos. In August 2026 it was affected by a major exploit in which contemporaneous reporting estimated roughly USD 74-75 million in affected or attacker-controlled assets before the Cronos network was halted.
what_happened: On 2026-08-30, Tectonic was reported to have suffered an exploit on Cronos. Contemporary reporting described rapid manipulation of TONIC's price followed by borrowing against inflated collateral, but Tectonic had not published a final root-cause determination in the sources reviewed for this record. Roughly USD 6 million was reported bridged to Ethereum before the chain halt, while most remaining exploit-linked assets were stranded or frozen on Cronos. Frozen or stranded assets are not treated as recovered funds.
uncertainty_notes: Final confirmed loss, formal root cause, bad-debt allocation, recovery amount, lender impact and final protocol-remediation outcome were not established in the reviewed sources. The approximately USD 74-75 million figure is retained as a contemporaneous estimate, not a final confirmed loss.
notes: Canonicalized as a bounded current DeFi lending incident. Do not infer that Cronos, Crypto.com or the TONIC token itself was independently compromised beyond what incident evidence establishes.
